segments.text: Strawberries are berries. Well, that's not exactly true. Botanically, they're not berries at all. But bananas are.
To a botanist, a berry is a fruit that grows from one flower with one ovary, with the seeds inside the flesh.
Bananas fit perfectly. So do grapes, tomatoes, kiwis, and even eggplants.
Here's the wild part. Those little dots on a strawberry aren't seeds. Each one is its own tiny fruit, with a seed inside.
That's not all. Raspberries and blackberries aren't true berries either. But pumpkins and watermelons? Technically, a kind of berry.
So next time you eat a strawberry, remember: the banana is the real berry.
